problem: Foundation-model VLN agents passively consume redundant panoramic inputs (visual token inflation, attention diffusion over irrelevant features) and reason over all historical waypoints/contexts without prioritization, obscuring instruction-critical fine-grained cues.
motivation: Reliable navigation decisions need the right fine-grained visual attributes (color, texture, spatial relations) and the right history. Long trajectories dilute LLM attention, so agents need to decide what to perceive and which past waypoints matter.
key_idea: A training-free LLM+VLM framework where an orchestration agent actively queries a VLM on focused regions of a text-based ego-centric semantic map, and Branch-Diverse MCTS filters top-k high-value historical waypoints for the decision agent to reason over.
insight: Ablations show both parts matter: removing proactive perception hurts most on R2R (SPL 41.2->30.0 for DS3+GLM; REVERIE OSR 57.14->36.0), while removing BD-MCTS mainly lowers OSR (R2R 63.0->54.2; REVERIE 57.14->42.67) and raises NE, implying weaker exploration and backtracking. Removing BD-MCTS on REVERIE slightly raises SPL (25.85->26.73), suggesting shorter but less successful paths. The qualitative cases show targeted queries correct wrong waypoint values, and top-k history enables error-correcting backtracking.
method: Ego-centric semantic map: the panorama is split into K overlapping views, a VLM detects objects with bounding boxes, SAM2 gives masks, monocular depth gives distances, and heading is computed from box position; all of it is serialized as text ('turn left/right h degrees, obj at d meters').

Reasoning-driven perception loop: the orchestration LLM gets the map, trajectory caption, instruction and query history, and emits a visual query plus a focused region; the perception VLM answers on the cropped region; the loop repeats until the LLM judges the information sufficient.

Semantic value estimation: after the loop, the orchestration LLM scores each newly discovered waypoint V_sem in [0,1] from the instruction, trajectory and accumulated descriptions; this replaces MCTS rollouts.

BD-MCTS expansion and backpropagation: a search tree over discovered waypoints (cross-branch nodes skipped to keep it acyclic) initializes Q with V_sem; the reward (mean value of new nodes, else Q(v_t)) is propagated along the root-to-current path with incremental-mean updates.

Top-k selection with branch diversity: leaves are scored by the visit-count weighted path-aggregated value minus lambda times the normalized graph distance; the top-k are chosen with at most 2 children per parent.

Focused decision agent: the decision LLM reasons over the top-k candidates, retrieving each candidate's historical context from the memory bank along its root path, together with the current multimodal context, and picks the next waypoint (including backtracking); the trajectory caption is then rebuilt.

setting.backbone: Orchestration and decision agents: DeepSeek-V3 or Qwen3-Max (frozen LLMs); perception agent: GLM-4.5V or Qwen3-VL-Max (frozen VLMs); plus a VLM detector, SAM2 and Depth Pro-style monocular depth
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (split into overlapping views), with monocular depth estimated and object masks from SAM2
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph waypoints (navigable candidates, with backtracking to historical waypoints)
setting.privileged: none stated (navigation graph discovered online; REVERIE evaluated on navigation only, no object grounding)

numbers_note: Evaluation is on an unspecified random subset of val-unseen. Ablation tables print R2R Q3+Q3VL SR as 52.0 (main table 52.5). Long-trajectory results (30 longest R2R episodes: Q3+Q3VL 50.0% SR, DS3+GLM 46.7%) are only in a figure and text.
results: ProFocus reaches 52.5% SR / 39.8% SPL on an R2R val-unseen subset (Q3+Q3VL) and 50.0% SR / 41.2% SPL (DS3+GLM), beating re-implemented NavGPT (Q3: 47.0/38.4) and MapGPT (GLM: 41.4/30.8), and published GPT-4-based zero-shot methods such as MSNav (46.0 SR, 40.0 SPL). On REVERIE it gets 40.0% SR (vs MapGPT GLM 37.1), while its DS3+GLM SR (36.9) is slightly below MapGPT (GLM).
limitations: Evaluated only on random val-unseen subsets with re-implemented baselines, not the full splits; the subset size is unspecified and the gains are small on REVERIE (DS3+GLM SR is below MapGPT).
Heavy pipeline (detector, SAM2, depth, multiple LLM/VLM calls per step, iterative loop) with no reported cost/latency analysis; no comparison to trained specialists (DUET etc. remain much stronger).
Only simulation, navigation-graph-based settings; no real-robot or continuous-environment tests; REVERIE object grounding is not evaluated.
